title: DC-area forecast: Toasty and humid today, with scattered storms possible late
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Partly to mostly cloudy and humid, with afternoon highs in the mid-80s to near 90. Storms become more likely heading into the evening.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Partly cloudy and humid, with afternoon highs in the mid-80s to near 90. Storms become more likely heading into the evening.

What’s next? Scattered storms, some potentially strong, are with us this evening into the early overnight. Sunnier Friday and still rather humid, maybe an isolated storm. Turning hotter this weekend into next week.

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: Humidity is up to uncomfortable levels. Plus, there’s heat and a storm chance. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Thursday): Clouds are more numerous today. We could see a couple of showers around this morning into midafternoon, but nothing too long-lasting or intense. Much of the day is dry as highs reach the mid-80s to near 90 and dew points rise toward 70. Odds of scattered storms grow late afternoon, but most activity should hold off until after 5 p.m. or so. Winds are from the south and southwest around 10 mph, with some gusts near 15 to 20 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: Scattered showers and storms are possible through the evening. Highest odds in our area run from about 6 p.m. to midnight, which may help keep storms from being too intense given that this comes well after peak heating. Still, isolated damaging winds, hail, or flooding could be an issue with a few storms. Overnight lows end up around 65 to 70 as some patchy fog develops. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): The front should sink far enough to our south to allow partly to mostly sunny skies, helping push highs into the mid- and upper 80s. Not as humid as today, but still rather humid with dew points well into the 60s, with an isolated shower or storm possible. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly clear, with lows ranging across the 60s. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

Warming up this weekend as we see lots of sunshine. Highs in the mid- and upper 80s Saturday, then mid-80s to around 90 Sunday, with moderate humidity. Odds of rain either day are pretty low as of now. Confidence: Medium

The most significant change heading into the workweek is increased heat. Near 90 to mid-90s both Monday and Tuesday, with sunny skies still the rule. Similar Wednesday, but perhaps with a late-day storm chance. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 27

Tropical Storm Doria in 1971 dumped record rainfall, causing deadly flooding that inundated roads, homes, and basements across the region.
